refusals.refusal: streams (cudaStreamCreate) is not in the C2M-T1 runtime subset; refusing rather than pretending it is a no-op
asynchronous copies (cudaMemcpyAsync) is not in the C2M-T1 runtime subset; refusing rather than pretending it is a no-op

device memset (cudaMemset) is not in the C2M-T1 runtime subset; refusing rather than pretending it is a no-op
host statement outside the C2M-T1 subset: 'int x = foo();'. Supported: cudaMalloc, cudaMemcpy (H2D/D2H), kernel<<<g,b>>>(...), cudaDeviceSynchronize, cudaFree, and a scalar host-array store.
kernel 'vadd' reads device buffer(s) ['d_a', 'd_b'] that were allocated but never written. CUDA leaves that memory uninitialised; refusing rather than silently reading zeros.

the_hazard.guard_refusal: host buffer 'h_a' is written AFTER being copied to the device, at 'h_a[0] = 999.0f;'. In CUDA that copy is a snapshot and the write does not reach the device; aliasing would make it a live reference and change the answer. Refusing to delete the copy for this program.

result.headline_DELETING_THE_COPY_IS_NOT_UNCOND: S015 §9 says to delete a CUDA-era concept that is unnecessary on Apple Silicon, and §125 calls unified memory a weapon. Both are right and there is a CONDITION nothing in this program had stated: in CUDA a host-to-device copy is a SNAPSHOT, and an alias is a LIVE REFERENCE. A program that writes its host buffer after the copy and before the launch gets a DIFFERENT ANSWER. Demonstrated, not asserted: the same host program gives -0.833595 under the faithful semantics and 998.529053 under aliasing, a divergence of 999.36 in EXACTLY ONE ELEMENT with every other element bit-identical -- which is the worst shape a bug can have, since an aggregate check would pass. may_delete_copies() refuses the optimization for such a program and NAMES the offending statement. The guard is bypassable only by a private flag used here and in its test, because a refusal nobody has watched be NECESSARY is indistinguishable from one that is merely cautious.
result.what_the_deletion_buys: At program level the faithful port and the unified native path agree BIT-FOR-BIT on every safe program, and the unified path performs ZERO copies against the port's THREE. Deleting them is worth 1.69x at 2^20 and 1.73x at 2^22, the latter with clean arms (2.45% / 8.39% IQR).
result.relationship_to_P6: P6 measured host<->device copying at 7.4x in a MICROBENCHMARK of the copy itself. This measures the same elimination inside a TRANSLATED PROGRAM, where the kernel work and the host-side interpretation are also in the arm, so 1.7x is the honest program-level figure and 7.4x is the honest cost-of-the-copy figure. Neither supersedes the other and quoting 7.4x as what a port gains would be wrong.
result.T2_is_blocked_by_the_FRONTEND_not_the_BA: AIR now has GEMM, reduction, scan, softmax and attention. NONE is reachable through C2M: the kernel parser handles 4 elementwise expression forms and cannot express a loop, shared memory or a barrier, so it cannot express any of them. T2 is a FRONTEND obligation and saying so keeps the backend's coverage from being read as C2M coverage.
result.a_third_harness_defect_found_and_fixed: The first run of this comparison returned NO_CLAIM at both sizes. The cause was the same class of mistake as the mx.eval-per-level defect: the timed function rebuilt the host numpy arrays on every call, putting a 16 MiB memcpy inside BOTH arms. Common-mode, so it did not bias the direction -- it DILUTED the margin and added noise until the gate refused a real result. Hoisting it is legitimate because the SAFE program never mutates h_a or h_b, and with it the same comparison gives 1.69x and 1.73x. THREE TIMES NOW the instrument has been the thing under measurement; the pattern is that any per-call setup inside an arm is suspect, whether it biases or merely blunts.

claim_boundary: C2M-T1 as this module defines it: cudaMalloc, cudaMemcpy H2D and D2H, a <<<grid,block>>> launch, cudaDeviceSynchronize and cudaFree, over elementwise T0 kernels. NOT CUDA runtime support -- streams, events, async copies, managed memory, memset, 2-D copies, device-to-device copies and multi-device selection are all REFUSED BY NAME. The launch geometry is PARSED AND IGNORED: AIR chooses its own grid, so a kernel whose result depends on blockDim would be mistranslated and this subset cannot express one. Oracle is numpy, not CUDA, so P2 stays open and this is not a differential.
